chapter: Stuff Smith, 52nd Street and session work
title: Stuff Smith's personality, drinking and the White Rose bar
summary: Stuff's drinking made him play better; musicians gathered at the White Rose before work at the Onyx.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: How did you get along with Stuff? He was quite a character.

Oh yeah, oh yeah. Stuff was just great. Stuff didn't do any harm to anybody but himself. He was just great, you know. We got along swell. Got along swell. He's one of the greatest jazz violinists I've ever heard in my life. He and Joe Venuti, they were just great. Yeah, I got along wonderful with Stuff, and in the band, all the guys got along with Stuff.
How did you come up with all those routines? Did you rehearse them or did they just come about on the stands?

No, a lot of times we would rehearse. It's a funny thing, this is a little something about Stuff that everybody knew Stuff used to drink a lot, you know, but you'd never see Stuff drunk so he couldn't play. So one night we were all up on the bandstand and things weren't sounding just right, you know. So Jonah and I used to sit right next to him, you know, sort of where you could turn around and say something to me and Jonah. So then, he says, 'Are we sounding all right tonight?' you know. And Jonah and I said 'Yes, Stuff, it sounds good.' So Stuff would look at me and say, 'Cozy, are you high?' I'd say 'no.' 'Jonah, are you high?' 'No.' Well then Stuff turned around and said 'Oh man, that's what wrong, everybody ain't high by 12:00 I'm going to fine you five dollars.' And anyway--
Drinking. So anyway, there used to be a bar right at the corner of 52nd and Sixth Avenue. All

the boys used to stop by and have a little taste, everybody. Roy Eldridge, Charlie Shavers, Kirby, Maxine Sullivan, Billie Pearl Bailey, everybody stop by, fifteen cent a drink, you know, go over there and get a little taste before coming to work. So, the owners of the Onyx club was Joe Helbock, and he and his wife used to sit right there in a little booth as you'd come in the front door. Well the White Rose was about from here to that tree away from the Onyx Club. Well in the White Rose it's close.
That was on the corner of 52nd and 6th.

Yeah, Sixth Avenue. And the Onyx was right around the corner. First club. So by being all fenced in there, you could smell all that whiskey on your clothes, you know. So anyway, like, we'd all meet there at the White Rose, come and have a taste, some of us wouldn't. But anyway, when you would come in the club on your clothes you could smell maybe a little whiskey or something, the aroma from the whiskey and all. So they used to say, 'uh uh, it's going to be a good night tonight 'cause they all high. Wait until about 12 or one o'clock and boy it's going to be a good night.' And just as sure as ever, around twelve, one o'clock it was a good night, everybody up there just high--not drunk you know, just Stuff he's high, and the higher he would get, the better he could play.
